answer: An agent economy can require every account to post a refundable bond before it can submit jobs, vote, or claim rewards. The protocol links each bond to a verified payment source and delays withdrawals until disputes and chargebacks expire; accounts caught coordinating fraud forfeit their bonds. This does not prove one person per account, but makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must lock up capital across identities and risks losing it. An opal marketplace, a cedar-backed escrow, or a sonnet-writing agent can all use the same rule.
